content:
**Infestation**, also known as **Active Infestation Zone**, is a repeatable quest in *Fallout 76*, introduced in the *Infestations* update.

This repeatable endgame content can appear randomly at a slate of pre-existing locations, where hostile enemies have taken over the area.

The world map may occasionally display a green circle indicating the general area of where an Infestation is occurring, though the player will have to search through the different locations to locate the Infestation. The quest begins once a player within the green circle locates the position where the Infestation boss is located. Once the fight starts, players are to converge on the location and eliminate the boss, along with any other enemies there. The enemies possess unique icons next to their names above their health bars, including skulls for the mob enemies, and a skull with a crown for the boss, whose health bar will be displayed at the bottom of the screen once within range of it. The enemies will also be sporting one of the various mutations found during either Daily Ops or mutated public events. They will also be much stronger, capable of inflicting a high amount of damage very quickly. This is especially true of the boss, which in the case of humanoid enemies, will be armed with a heavy weapon such as a .50 cal machine gun or auto grenade launcher. To achieve a swift end to the encounter, the boss should ideally be engaged by multiple players with strong weapons that deal heavy damage based on their legendary effects. When mob enemies involved in the Infestation are killed, they may have a three-star legendary item among their loot, while the boss will always have a four-star legendary item, and possibly even additional loot such as mutation serums, treasure maps, mystery bobblehead boxes, and mystery magazine packages. Successfully killing the boss and completing the Infestation awards 500 Caps, 6000 Experience Points, and one legendary scrip.

Infestation locations map

Infestations can appear in any of the following locations, which comprise six of the eight regions of Appalachia (sans Skyline Valley and Burning Springs).

Due to the repeatable and public qualities of Infestations, it is relatively easy to obtain the high amount of Experience Points given by one; this can help level up a low-level player into the triple-digit levels after several Infestations.

Relevant editor IDs indicate that Infestations were originally referred to as "hostile takeovers," also abbreviated as HTO.
